summary: Evaluation of 14 days of Nightscout telemetry and AAPS settings shows an overall time-in-range of 86.0% with strong nocturnal stability, though punctuated by mild-to-moderate overnight dipping (5.1% below range) and late-afternoon postprandial surges. Zero manual carb entries are present, with the closed loop relying entirely on UAM detection, smb_always_enabled=true, and a flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U scaled by dynamic sensitivity.
issues: Late-afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia (averaging 148 to 163 mg/dL between 15:00 and 17:00 local time) due to reactive-only UAM/SMB delivery without manual meal announcement.
Recurrent nocturnal and early-morning glucose dipping (10% to 18.5% time below range between 00:00 and 02:00 local time) indicating slightly aggressive overnight basal rates.
Absence of manual carbohydrate logging, requiring the automation system to absorb all postprandial response demands reactively.
education: UAM (Unannounced Meal) detection allows AAPS to respond to unexpected glucose rises, but reactive dosing inherently lags behind food absorption compared to prebolusing or announced meals.
Maintaining a flat ISF profile across all hours can mask time-of-day sensitivity variations, forcing dynamic sensitivity and safety multipliers to overcompensate.
strengths: Excellent CGM data quality with 98.7% coverage and robust telemetry logging over the 14-day evaluation period.
High overall time-in-range (86.0%) and effective closed-loop automation handling unannounced meals safely.
safety_notes: TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.
The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is 98.7% with 3,995 valid entries and minimal gaps. Telemetry is rich with over 2,300 treatments and 6,200 device statuses.
analysis_steps.evidence: CGM entry count 3,995, raw entry count 3,995, coverage percent 98.7, largest gap 65 minutes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero explicit carb entries logged in Nightscout treatments.

analysis_steps.findings: Mean glucose is 121.6 mg/dL with 86.0% time in range, 8.9% time above range, and 5.1% time below range. Hypoglycemia occurs primarily in overnight and early-morning hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: Glucose summary average 121.6 mg/dL, SD 39.7 mg/dL, TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates (0.6 to 0.7 U/h) contribute to mild nocturnal dipping, while afternoon hours show consistent postprandial elevation requiring better prandial or basal alignment.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly glucose local 00:00-02:00 shows up to 18.5% time below range; 15:00-17:00 shows average glucose 148-163 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of manual carb entries limits precise evaluation of prandial insulin requirements versus basal adequacy.

analysis_steps.findings: Active ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U with a 10-hour DIA. Dynamic sensitivity is active at 70%, compensating for a rigid profile foundation.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.isf_segments lists 56 mg/dL/U; dia_hours is 10.0; dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent is 70%.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Flat ISF structure lacks time-of-day granularity.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled with smb_always_enabled=true, perfectly matching a workflow without manual carb entries.
Autosens is disabled while dynamic sensitivity is active at 70%. Safety limits (max basal 12 U/h, max IOB 25 U) are wide but safe relative to observed IOB peaks under 6 U.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true, max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h, max_iob_units=25 U.

analysis_steps.findings: Without manual carb entries, meals rely entirely on UAM and SMB reactive microbolusing, leading to predictable afternoon postprandial peaks.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_treatment_entries is empty, treatment_summary.carb_entries is 0, hourly glucose peaks in afternoon hours.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact meal carb amounts and timing unrecorded.

analysis_steps.findings: Extended carbs and e-carbs are not utilized. Carb absorption model uses default 7-hour max absorption and 8 mg/dL/5 min minimum impact.
analysis_steps.evidence: extended_carb_entries is 0, meal_max_absorption_hours is 7 h, min_5m_carbimpact is 8 mg/dL/5 min.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb or extended absorption data present.

analysis_steps.findings: Evidence supports keeping current profile and automation settings while recommending manual meal logging as a primary behavioral step to evaluate prandial efficacy before making insulin parameter adjustments.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overall 86% TIR, stable closed-loop operation, and absence of manual carb entries.

recommendations.title: Introduce Manual Carbohydrate Logging
recommendations.description: Log manual carbohydrate entries for significant meals for at least 3 consecutive days to evaluate whether current carb ratios and ISF provide accurate automated dosing when meal timing is explicitly known.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Current basal rates maintain an 86.0% TIR and stable overnight profiles, though minor nocturnal dipping (5.1% TBR) exists. Because zero manual carb entries are logged, adjusting insulin parameters before establishing baseline meal-announced data risks confounding closed-loop behavior.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor nocturnal glucose and daytime postprandial excursions for 3 consecutive days after initiating manual carbohydrate logging.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings unchanged while initiating manual meal logging to assess automated response accuracy.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight basal maintains overall stability; nocturnal dipping is mild and does not currently warrant a profile change prior to logging meal data. Evidence: nocturnal TIR high, minor dipping 00:00-02:00. Uncertainty: unannounced meal residue or variable late-evening digestion. Dependencies: none.
Morning baseline is stable with good fasting time in range. Evidence: hourly glucose 05:00-07:00 averages ~99 mg/dL. Uncertainty: none. Dependencies: none.

Mid-day basal segment supports fasting intervals adequately. Evidence: stable mid-day glucose. Uncertainty: unannounced snacks. Dependencies: none.

Afternoon peaks are driven by unannounced meal absorption rather than basal deficiency. Evidence: reactive UAM/SMB handling unannounced intake. Uncertainty: exact meal timing. Dependencies: manual meal logging.
Evening basal rate is appropriate for evening transition. Evidence: stable evening glucose averages. Uncertainty: none. Dependencies: none.
Late evening basal rate maintains stability prior to midnight. Evidence: good evening time in range. Uncertainty: none. Dependencies: none.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Safety limits prevent hard throttling while observed IOB peaks remain well within safe thresholds (<6 U). Evidence: max IOB in telemetry ~5.9 U. Uncertainty: none. Dependencies: none.

Dynamic sensitivity with a 70% adjustment factor successfully provides necessary insulin scaling without requiring autosens. Evidence: responsive correction windows. Uncertainty: none. Dependencies: none.
Default absorption parameters function effectively alongside UAM detection. Evidence: stable loop predictions. Uncertainty: unannounced meal composition. Dependencies: manual meal logging.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: While maintaining closed-loop automation (smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true), introduce manual carbohydrate entry for significant meals to allow prebolusing or prompt announced dosing, which will flatten late-afternoon postprandial peaks.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: In the total absence of manual carb entries, the loop relies entirely on reactive UAM detection and microbolusing, causing predictable postprandial hyperglycemia before insulin action catches up.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log manual carbohydrate entries for at least 3 consecutive days to evaluate automated response accuracy under announced meal conditions.

exceptions.pattern: Late-afternoon postprandial surges (15:00 to 17:00 local time)
exceptions.suggestion: Consider initiating a temporary target or small manual bolus prior to known recurring meal times.
exceptions.rationale: Reactive UAM/SMB dosing initiates insulin action only after glucose begins rising, causing temporary excursions above target.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Continue closed-loop operation with current profile settings and AAPS automation parameters.
Step 2: Begin logging manual carbohydrate entries for all significant meals over the next 3 to 5 days.
Step 3: Review postprandial glucose curves and time-in-range following meal announcements before considering any profile or ISF adjustments.
